fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: When the soft tissue inside a tooth becomes infected or inflamed, it can cause significant pain and, if left untreated, lead to an abscess. Root canal therapy aims to remove the source of infection and preserve your natural tooth.

fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: At Precision Dental, we understand that the words root canal can cause concern. We explain every step, prioritise your comfort and use modern techniques to make treatment as efficient as possible.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Is Root Canal Therapy?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Inside every tooth is a space containing the dental pulp, made up of nerves and blood vessels. This space extends down through narrow channels within the roots, known as root canals. Deep decay, cracks, repeated dental work or injury can allow bacteria to reach the pulp, causing inflammation or infection.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Root canal therapy, also called endodontic treatment, involves removing the damaged pulp, cleaning and disinfecting the canals, and sealing them to reduce the risk of reinfection. The tooth is then restored, often with a crown, to protect it.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Is Root Canal Therapy Right for You?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Root canal therapy may be recommended if you have:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A severe or throbbing toothache

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Lingering sensitivity to hot or cold

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Pain when biting or chewing

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Swelling or tenderness in the gums near a tooth

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A pimple-like bump on the gum

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A darkened tooth following injury

fields.label: List item
fields.value: An infection visible on an X-ray, even without symptoms

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The main alternative is removal of the tooth. We will discuss the benefits, risks and costs of both options so you can decide what is right for you. In complex cases, referral to an endodontist may be recommended.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Diagnosis

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We examine the tooth, perform sensitivity tests and take digital X-rays to understand the extent of the problem. If treatment is needed, we explain the process and provide a quote.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Relieving Pain and Cleaning the Canals

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Local anaesthetic is used to numb the area. A protective sheet called a rubber dam isolates the tooth and keeps it clean. We then gently remove the infected pulp and shape and disinfect the canals using rotary endodontic instruments, which help us work efficiently through narrow and curved canals. A medicated dressing and temporary filling are placed.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Filling the Canals

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: At a following visit, once symptoms have settled, the canals are filled with a biocompatible material and sealed.

fields.label: Subheading
fields.value: Restoring the Tooth

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Teeth that have had root canal therapy can become brittle, so a crown is often recommended to protect the tooth. In many cases, this can be completed with a CEREC same-day crown.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Your tooth may feel tender for a few days after each visit, which can usually be managed with over-the-counter pain relief. Avoid chewing hard foods on the tooth until it has been fully restored. Contact us if you notice increasing pain, swelling or if your temporary filling comes out. Maintain good oral hygiene and attend regular check-ups.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for Root Canal Therapy

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for Root Canal Therapy

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We use rubber dam isolation, digital X-rays and rotary endodontic instruments to support careful, efficient treatment. Our team keeps you informed throughout, and happy gas is available if you would like extra support to relax.

sections.label: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Small label
fields.value: FAQ

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Is root canal therapy painful?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Treatment is performed under local anaesthetic. Many patients find the procedure similar to having a filling, and it often relieves the pain caused by infection.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How many appointments will I need?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Most root canal treatments take two or more visits, depending on the tooth, the number of canals and how the infection responds.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Why do I need a crown after root canal therapy?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Root-treated teeth, particularly back teeth, can become weaker and more likely to fracture. A crown helps protect the tooth.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: What happens if I do not have treatment?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: An infected tooth will not heal on its own. The infection may spread, causing a dental abscess, and the tooth may eventually need removal.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Is it better to remove the tooth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Keeping your natural tooth is often preferable, but it depends on the condition of the tooth. We will discuss both options openly.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How successful is root canal therapy?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Many root-treated teeth function well for years, but outcomes vary. Factors include the complexity of the canals, the extent of infection and how the tooth is restored.
